newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Congress party told to pay tax.
newsitem.headline: India's Congress party told to pay tax.

text.p: India's Congress party has failed to file proper income tax accounts for the 1994/95 fiscal year on time and lost its right to an exemption, authorities said on Thursday.

The chief commissioner of income tax in Delhi, A.K. Batabyal, released a statement saying Congress had been told to pay tax for the year ended on March 31, 1995, because it failed to file proper accounts by the end of last month.
The statement said all other major political parties had submitted necessary income tax returns and statements of accounts for 1994/95 in accordance with a 1995 Supreme Court ruling.
It cited the Communist Party of India (Marxist), the Bharatiya Janata Party, the Janata Party and the Samajwadi Party, all of which were granted exemptions that the law provides to political parties.
"However, in the case of the Indian National Congress, despite several opportunities given, no proper accounts or verification of income and expenditure were received," the three-page statement said.
Congress spokesman Vithal Gadgil said the party would appeal against the notice by the income tax department and request more time to provide the necessary information.

"We will file an appeal against the notice and we will ask for time because we have more than 400 Congress committees all over the country," he told Reuters, saying the appeal would be lodged with the income tax tribunal.
Gadgil said Congress's central committee in New Delhi had filed proper accounts, but that its regional offices scattered across the country needed more time to comply.
Batabyal told Reuters that Congress had filed a 1994/95 income tax return in February 1996, but that it was not supported by proper documents.
The statement said Congress's income tax return showed that the party had received some donations from abroad.

"The party, even after utilising a number of adjourned hearings, could not submit the names and addresses of donors for over 10,000 rupees ($280)," it said, referring to the level above which donors have to be identified.
Batabyal said authorities had estimated Congress's 1994/95 income at about 250 million rupees. He did not say what the tax liability would be. ($1 = 35.8 rupees)
